**Source paper:** "Neural Enhancement of the Traditional Wang–Sheeley–Arge Solar Wind Relation," by Prateek Mayank, Enrico Camporeale, Arpit K. Shrivastav, Thomas E. Berger, and Charles N. Arge (arXiv:2509.06181v2).

**WSA velocity equation (Eq. 1 in the paper):**

V_wsa = V_min + V_max / (1 + f_s)^α × (1 − a1 · exp(−(D/w)^β))^a2

Here f_s is the flux-tube expansion factor at the source surface, and D is the minimum angular distance to the coronal hole boundary.

**Default coefficient set used in the paper:**

| Parameter | Default | Optimization bounds (Table 1) |
|---|---|---|
| V_min | 250 | [250, 300] |
| V_max | 750 | [600, 900] |
| α | 0.222 | [0.01, 0.5] |
| β | 1.25 | [0.01, 3.0] |
| w | 0.028 | [0.01, 0.05] |
| a1 | 0.8 | [0.7, 0.9] |
| a2 | 3 | [0.5, 6.5] |

The paper does not state units for the parameters. It implies km/s for the wind speeds, since it mentions a 500 km/s limit on V_min at 0.1 AU. It gives no units for w, α, β, a1, or a2.

**Attribution:** The paper says the defaults are "consistent with values used in previous studies" citing McGregor et al. (2011) and Reiss et al. (2019), and "several contemporary solar wind modeling" studies citing Pomoell & Poedts (2018) and Mayank et al. (2022). It does not attribute the coefficient set to a specific paper in a direct statement.

**Sources you requested that the content does not support:**
- **Riley (2015):** The paper cites Riley (2015) for re-examining the expansion-factor term, but it does not attribute any WSA coefficients to it. The reference list also has two near-identical Riley entries (refs. 25 and 26) with the same title and DOI.
- **Arge (2003):** Cited as the original WSA reference, with no coefficients attributed. **Arge (2004):** Not cited.
- **Wallace:** Not cited anywhere in the content.
- **Reiss:** Cited (Reiss et al. 2019, ApJS 240, 35) only as a prior source for the default values, with no coefficient details.

**Source:** S.J. Edwards, A.R. Yeates, F.-X. Bocquet, and D.H. Mackay, "Influence of Non-Potential Coronal Magnetic Topology on Solar-Wind Models" (arXiv:1511.00427). The journal is not named on the page.

**Equation (Eq. 8):**

v_r(θ,ϕ) = 240.0 + 675/(1+f_s)^{1/4.5} · [1.0 − 0.8·e^{(−(θ_b/1.9)²)}]³ km s⁻¹

**Coefficients:** 240.0, 675, exponent 1/4.5, 1.0, 0.8, 1.9, and cube (³).

**Radius of application:** The text says "radial wind speed at 21.5 R⊙ is determined by an empirical formula," so the formula applies at 21.5 R⊙ (0.1 AU).

**Variable definitions (quoted):**
- f_s: "measures the local radial expansion of a magnetic flux tube"
- θ_b: "is the angular distance of the field line's photospheric footpoint from the nearest coronal-hole boundary"

**Attribution sentences (quoted):**
- "one current implementation (based on GONG and NSO magnetograms) uses the formula"
- The source cites this as "(C.N. Arge, private communication)."
- "This is a slight modification of the formula discussed by" [Arge et al. 2004].
- "the numerical factors in this formula have been optimised to best match solar-wind observations for the PFSS model"

**Reference for Arge et al. 2004:** C.N. Arge, J.G. Luhmann, D. Odstrcil, C.J. Schrijver, and Y. Li, "Stream structure and coronal sources of the solar wind during the May 12th, 1997 CME," *J. Atmosph. Solar-Terrestrial Phys.* 66, 1295 (2004).

**McGregor 2011:** This page does not mention McGregor (2011), so I cannot provide any attribution from it.

I didn't find McGregor et al. (2011)'s actual coefficient values for w, β, 1/4.5, or 2/9, so I can't confirm them from these results.

- **What the paper covers:** It recalibrated the empirical WSA velocity relation at 0.1 AU so the output could feed ENLIL's inner boundary. The work arose from an attempt to better calibrate the empirical velocity relationship used in the Wang-Sheeley-Arge (WSA) model at 0.1 AU. It also was cross-validated using the 3D MHD code ENLIL and by comparing the results with observations at 1AU and at further distances as provided by Ulysses.
- **Helios link:** The same group used an empirical fit to historic Helios observations to set density at ENLIL's inner boundary, with temperature derived from constant thermal pressure.
- **Coefficient names:** A 2023 Frontiers paper says WSA-type models are the most widely used empirical models that predict the solar wind velocity at the lower boundary, citing McGregor et al. (2011) among others. A NASA paper notes the speed formula has several coefficients (β, γ, w, δ, Ao, ν1), which suggests w and β are standard WSA parameters. I did not confirm their values in McGregor (2011).
- **Possible source of 2/9:** A Frontiers result lists Merkin et al. (2011) with V_min = 200 km/s, V_max = 750 km/s, a1 = 2/9. That is a different paper using WSA coefficients, not McGregor et al. (2011), so it may not be what you need.

To get the exact values, check the full text of McGregor et al. (2011), *JGR Space Physics*, DOI 10.1029/2010JA015881, specifically its calibrated velocity equation and table of coefficients.

The review does not contain WSA coefficient sets for Arge 2003/2004, McGregor 2011, Riley 2015, Reiss 2019/2020, or Wallace. It cites Arge and Pizzo (2000), Arge et al. (2004), and McGregor et al. (2011) only as WS/WSA-type models, without listing their coefficients. The sets below are the ones it does give. It uses parameters a1 to a4 only, not a1 to a8.

**Generic WSA form (Eq. 2 in the paper):**

V_r = V_min + (V_max − V_min) / (1 + f_s)^a1 × [1 − 0.8·exp(−(θ_b/a2)^a3)]^a4

Here f_s is the magnetic expansion factor and θ_b is the minimum angular separation from the coronal hole boundary. V is in km/s.

**Coefficient sets stated in the review:**

| Pahud et al. 2012 | 240 | 675 | 2/9 | 2.8° | 1.25 | 3 | |
| Merkin et al. 2016 | 240 | 675 | 2/9 | 1.9° | 2 | 3 | Time-dependent ADAPT magnetograms |
| Wiengarten et al. 2014 | 200 | 675 | 2/9 | (2.8°, 3.2°) | 2 | 3 | a2 given as a range |
| Gonzi et al. 2021 (WSA option) | 240 | 675 | 2/9 | 2.8° | 1.25 | 3 | Same values as Pahud et al. 2012 |
| Pomoell & Poedts 2018 | 240 | 675 | 2/9 | 0.02 rad | 1.25 | 3 | 50 km/s subtracted afterward |
| Narechania et al. 2021 | 250 | 850 | 0.2 | 2.6° | 1.25 | 2.5 | |
| Mayank et al. 2022 | 250 | 650 | 2/9 | median of θ_bE | 1.25 | 3 | a2 set from field lines reaching Earth |
| Li et al. 2020 | 240 | 560 | 2/9 | 2° | 1 | 3 | |
| Shen et al. 2018; Wang et al. 2020 | not given | 675 | 0.22 rad | not given | 1.0 | 1.0 | V_min and a2 vary with solar cycle; no values stated |

**Related non-WSA forms in the review (for completeness):**

- Wiengarten et al. 2013 uses a different expression: V_min = 154, V_del = 300, V_xp = 3, α1 = 7.4 km/s, α2 = 3.5.
- Odstrcil 2003 (WS): V_min = 285, V_max = 575, α = 1/1.7.
- Shiota et al. 2014 (WS): V_min = 267.5, V_max = 410, α = 0.4.
- Detman et al. 2006 uses a WS-like form with V_min = 200, V_max = 700, V_xp = 1.5.

**Citation details for the source article:** Zhang, M., Feng, X., Li, H., Xiong, M., Shen, F., Yang, L., Zhao, X., Zhou, Y., & Liu, X. (2023). **Model description:** WSA (Wang-Sheeley-Arge) has three components:

1. **Inner corona (PFSS):** A potential field source surface model from the photosphere (1 solar radius) to the source surface (2.5 solar radii), built from a spherical harmonic expansion of the surface flux map.
2. **Current sheet (Schatten CS):** A pseudo-potential extension from 2.5 to 5 solar radii that forms a current sheet and helmet streamer above the global neutral line.
3. **Wind speed:** Speed at 5 solar radii is set by an empirical formula. The page says it depends on the "local rate of expansion of the magnetic flux tube" relative to a radial field, and on the footpoint's distance to the nearest coronal hole boundary.

**Version:** 5.4. The CCMC retired this model from its Continuous Runs System on December 8, 2025.

**Velocity equation and coefficients:** The page does not give the wind speed equation or its coefficients. It only describes the equation's inputs.

**References:**
- Arge, C.N. and Pizzo, V.J., *JGR*, 105, pp. 10465–10479 (2000), doi:10.1029/1999JA000262 (required citation for publications)
- Hickmann, K. S., Godinez, H. C., Henney, C. J., and Arge, C. N. (2015), "Data Assimilation in the ADAPT Photospheric Flux Transport Model," *Solar Physics*, 290, 1105–1118, doi:10.1007/s11207-015-0666-3
- ADAPT references: https://www.nso.edu/data/nisp-data/adapt-maps/

**Contacts:** Charles Nickolos Arge, NASA GSFC (model developer); Peter MacNeice, NASA GSFC CCMC (model host).

**WSA v5.2 (NASA CCMC)**

**Model description**
WSA has three components:
1. **PFSS (1 to 2.5 solar radii):** A potential field source surface model of the inner coronal magnetic field, built from a photospheric surface flux map with a spherical harmonic expansion.
2. **Schatten Current Sheet (2.5 to 5 solar radii):** A pseudo-potential extension that creates a thin current sheet and helmet streamer above the global neutral line.
3. **Empirical wind speed formula (at 5 solar radii):** Computes wind speed from the field solution there.

**Version:** v.5.2. The page header and title list this version. The page shows "Last Updated: 10/15/2026."

**Velocity equation and coefficients:** The page does not give the equation or its coefficients. It describes the formula only in general terms, as "an empirical formula which is a function of the local rate of expansion of the magnetic flux tube." It also depends on the footpoint's distance to the nearest coronal hole boundary.

**Radius of speed output**
- **5 solar radii:** The standard WSA outer boundary of the Current Sheet component.
- **21.5 solar radii:** Required if the run is meant to produce a coronal field solution for an ENLIL run.

**Version history and coefficient notes:** The page contains no version history and no coefficient values.

**References**
- Arge, C.N. and Pizzo, V.J., *JGR*, 105, pp. 10465–10479 (2000), doi:10.1029/1999JA000262. This is the paper to cite for the model.
- Hickmann, K.S., Godinez, H.C., Henney, C.J., and Arge, C.N. (2015), "Data Assimilation in the ADAPT Photospheric Flux Transport Model," *Solar Physics*, 290, 1105–1118, doi:10.1007/s11207-015-0666-3. This covers the ADAPT magnetogram inputs.

**Contacts:** Charles Nickolos Arge (NASA GSFC, model developer) and Peter MacNeice (NASA GSFC CCMC, model host).

The page doesn't contain the parameters you asked about. It has no details on g53q5, the a6b1/a3b2 ambient settings, the d4t1x1 cone model parameters, or the vfast, vslow, dfast, tfast, bfast, xalpha, and velocity reduction defaults. It also doesn't describe the inner boundary conditions beyond the summary below.

**What the page says about ENLIL 2.8f**

- **Inner boundary:** "Its inner radial boundary is located beyond the sonic point, typically at 21.5 or 30 solar radii."
- **Boundary input:** It can take boundary conditions from either the WSA or MAS model.
- **Outer boundary:** Adjustable to include planets or spacecraft, for example 2 AU for Earth and Mars, 5 AU for Ulysses, or 10 AU for Cassini.
- **Grid coverage:** 60° north to 60° south in latitude and 360° in azimuth.
- **Method:** A time-dependent 3D MHD model using a Flux-Corrected-Transport (FCT) algorithm, written in Fortran.

**References**

- Odstrcil, D. (2003). Modeling 3-D solar wind structure. *Advances in Space Research* 32, 497–506. https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/S0273-1177(03)00332-6
